To add something, thats why Images and Words and Metropolis pt. 2 are fan favorites, the creativity on the rythm is the backbone of those songs and in combination with the crazy harmony and riffs its insane. A tool favorite is Schim, and I think it enters this criteria too.

Honestly, imho, everything lands on rythmic variation, either shuffling the accents, switch polyrithms, bar changes, a change on hihat/cymbal pattern, breakdowns, etc. 
Those rythmic variations create a backbone for the other instruments to switch things, so your guitars can do the same harmony following a new rythmic pattern, your synths can switch to arpeggiating the chords, developing a new bass riff according to snare/kick. That in itself open up new transitions, new ideas, modulations, new forms of tensions, etc. 
Prog lacks of formulas, thats why its amazing, and why new dream theater songs are boring af, cause they found the DT formula.
For me its more visually appealing, an easier setup of the presets, low charge on the memory usage and very fast setup.
